correctness.rationale: For fixed binary pattern v, greedy first occurrence time is a sum of independent geometric waiting times whose PGF is product of g_symbol; counting each distinct pattern once yields occurrence generating weight product(g_i)/(1−z). At Abelian half-length L and j zeros per half there are C(L,j)^2 patterns, contributing g0^(2j)g1^(2(L−j)); the classical Laurent constant-term identity gives exactly the displayed bivariate inverse-square-root PGF (excluding L=0). Factor radical at u=1 as (1−(g0+g1)^2)(1−(g0−g1)^2); unique dominant radius r=1/(1+t), t=√(p(1−p)), with r(g0+g1)'=2(1+t)/(1+2t). Transfer of its square-root singularity gives E[A_n]~[(1+2t)√(1+t)/(4√π t^(3/2))](1+t)^n/√n, and a separate simple pole gives the unrestricted expectation. The final ratio has √((1+t)/(4πtn)); deterministic p endpoints handled separately, not conflated with the fixed-interior limit. Independent exact host enumeration at n≤8, p=1/2,1/3 reproduces initial moments, not the infinite singularity argument.
